corrections.text: The article quotes ChatGPT Work as "constructed on Codex and powered by GPT-5.6." This phrase does not appear verbatim in the cited Thurrott article. Thurrott's own commentary (not an OpenAI quote) instead says, in two separate sentences, that ChatGPT Work "is built on Codex" and separately "It's powered by the GPT-5.6 frontier model." The quoted phrase is a paraphrase and should not have been presented in quotation marks.

The article states the June executive order "requir[es] companies to submit powerful models for government review 30 days before public release." The cited Engadget source describes the order as one that "asks companies to voluntarily present their most powerful models for government review" 30 days before release — a voluntary framework, not a mandatory requirement. The Machine Herald's own July 5 article on the same order correctly described it as "requesting that AI companies voluntarily submit" their models.
